subject.title: fix(memory-core): preserve sibling supplement results when one search rejects (#77897)

question: Should memory corpus supplements have a fixed 10-second per-supplement cutoff inside the existing 15-second whole-tool deadline?
rationale: The cutoff bounds hung supplements and permits partial results, but it intentionally changes successful behavior for supplements that settle between 10 and 15 seconds, so the timing contract requires feature-owner judgment.

options.title: Keep the fixed cutoff
options.body: Accept the stricter 10-second supplement contract and require latest-head live proof of partial and total failure behavior.

options.title: Unify deadline ownership
options.body: Derive supplement cancellation from the whole-tool deadline or an abort-aware SDK contract so timing policy has one owner.

options.title: Pause for an SDK seam
options.body: Hold the PR until the supplement API supports an explicit abort or deadline signal.

recommendation.title: Keep the fixed cutoff
recommendation.body: Accept the stricter 10-second supplement contract and require latest-head live proof of partial and total failure behavior.

likelyOwner.reason: He introduced the current memory-core tool runner and supplement aggregation behavior in commit 8f893416.
